request.query: A projection of polynomial coefficient support preserves upper bounds for coordinate exponents; supremum on image support is bounded by original supremum.

items.informal_name: Monomial Exponent Bounded by Total Degree in Multivariate Polynomial
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] (i : σ) {f : MvPolynomial σ R} {m : σ →₀ ℕ},
  m ∈ f.support → m i ≤ MvPolynomial.degreeOf i f
items.informal_description: For any variable $i$ in $\sigma$, multivariate polynomial $f \in R[\sigma]$, and monomial $m$ in the support of $f$ (i.e., with nonzero coefficient), the exponent of $i$ in $m$ satisfies $m_i \leq \deg_i(f)$, where $\deg_i(f)$ denotes the total degree of $f$ in variable $i$ (sum of exponents of $i$ across all monomials in $f$).

items.informal_name: Degree of Variable in Polynomial ≤ d iff All Monomials Have Degree ≤ d
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] {n : σ} {f : MvPolynomial σ R} {d : ℕ},
  MvPolynomial.degreeOf n f ≤ d ↔ ∀ m ∈ f.support, m n ≤ d
items.informal_description: For a multivariate polynomial $ f $ over a commutative semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $, and for a variable $ n \in \sigma $ and a natural number $ d $, the degree of $ n $ in $ f $ is less than or equal to $ d $ if and only if every monomial in the support of $ f $ has the exponent of $ n $ less than or equal to $ d $.

items.informal_name: Degree of a variable in a multivariate polynomial equals the supremum over its support
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] (n : σ) (f : MvPolynomial σ R),
  MvPolynomial.degreeOf n f = f.support.sup fun m => m n
items.informal_description: For a multivariate polynomial $ f $ over a commutative semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $, and for a variable $ n \in \sigma $, the degree of $ n $ in $ f $ is equal to the supremum of the exponents of $ n $ in the monomials of $ f $. This is formally expressed as $ \deg_n(f) = \sup_{m \in \text{supp}(f)} m(n) $, where $ \text{supp}(f) $ denotes the support of $ f $.

items.informal_name: Support Exponents are Bounded by Polynomial Degree
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Semiring R] {p : Polynomial R}, ∀ a ∈ p.support, ↑a ≤ p.degree
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ p $ over a semiring $ R $, if a natural number $ a $ is in the support of $ p $, then $ a \leq \deg(p) $.

items.informal_name: Supremum Degree Equals Maximum under Degree Function
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {A : Type u_3} {B : Type u_5} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : SemilatticeSup B] [inst_2 : OrderBot B]
  {D : A → B} [inst_3 : AddZeroClass A] {p : AddMonoidAlgebra R A} {b : B},
  b ∈ Set.range D → Function.invFun D b ∈ p.support → (∀ a ∈ p.support, D a ≤ b) → AddMonoidAlgebra.supDegree D p = b
items.informal_description: If $ b $ is in the range of the degree function $ D $, the preimage $ D^{-1}(b) $ is in the support of $ p $, and $ b $ is an upper bound for $ D(a) $ for all $ a $ in the support of $ p $, then the supremum degree of $ p $ with respect to $ D $ is equal to $ b $. Formally, $ \supDegree_D(p) = b $.
